# D3b native war, occupation and suspended ally exports

These four files are byte-identical public exports from real UI continuations of the D3a campaign SHA `608b238c20d8e7c50fa51069b9b0b84cffae4ea6be8954b9e937ca767c4e3500`. The production build was `index-DfiMAwYb.js` (SHA `a61e971a19f2d73fd7cb1fb5c7ae1c9c8cdc1665225f0d063fe17e0274eb4c71`) with `index-DDhTxvxv.css` (SHA `659a71458cfef637d4311c1c38e4a143b8b855c8cb856aacb2953c9aa489f094`). No fixture payload was edited.

The main route deliberately declares war at the roots capital's orbit, wins an actual invasion with five paid pulses and then pays40 for a colony. The two-pulse export is actual military battle4: enemy36 health, player107 health, one received hit and no result yet. Military permission retains the winning claim W3 and founding receipt E32. Actual production supplies eight goods, sold at the neutral resin market for96. A mapped raid is physically defended before its deadline. A second genuine raid is deliberately ignored; its180-second deadline transfers ownership while preserving the colony, paid permission and existing stock. Eight more goods were loaded before expiry, leaving storage room so stopped production is measurable. The occupied export has health83, balance158, cargo8, produced17/loaded16 and one preserved stock item. The entire colony remained exact for ten ordinary economy seconds while its services were disabled.

The same colony is then recaptured in a second actual invasion. Its original ID and founding permission survive, production resumes, and explicit peace preserves ownership. After physical home docking, the eight carried goods sell for64. The canonical export is home with health67, balance222, empty goods cargo and the same colony now produced22/loaded16. It records two invasion victories, one defense victory, two raids, one expiry and one peace. There was no combat cash reward or extra healing. The original31 D3a economic receipts, all three pirate histories, paid ship model, modules, peaceful resin title, B2 and lineage remain unchanged.

The ally fixture is a separate ordinary branch from D3a, not a continuation replacing the canonical main campaign. War against resin suspends the existing paid ally24 with energy `5.9666666666668`, generated `55.80733333333501` and delivered `61.84066666666639`. Its ID, null location and exact account survive public rekey and actual movement. After60.4 real economic seconds, peace returns that same ally; only the bounded actual post-peace solar interval changes energy. The final independent branch is retained in browser evidence and the canonical campaign SHA remains unchanged.

Both in-space main fixtures retain complete domestic projection SHA `d98bf6179a237d7892f648e1a0b9df2c7336a516363f002f772e2cbf8811e028`, excluding only import IDs as documented by the native driver. Docking resumes domestic time, so this hash is not asserted against the final home export. All four historical generation checkpoints remain tick66066, pre-purchase, no ship or later colonies, empty independently activated wars, combat2 and economy5. Public import/rekey does not create a new generation checkpoint.

`space-war-fixtures.test.ts` verifies exact bytes, parser/export, local save/load, campaign rekey, older-checkpoint recovery, unchanged D3a history and actual military/occupation/ally identities. Its short ordinary-time battle, occupation and ally continuations and malformed copies are separately labelled unit regressions. The explicit `enableSpaceEvents` compatibility tests activate only empty D3c event histories and economy5→6 in live and older checkpoint states. They must not retroactively convert old cargo, battles, occupation or ecology into incidents, heal the ship or rewrite receipts. The original fixture bytes remain D3b/economy5 without events.

The native run used public UI, native RAF and unmodified public exports. Two harness failures remain documented rather than labelled successful: repeated imports exhausted isolated browser storage (separately reproduced; the original exception was masked by its download catch), and the final home sale initially targeted a panel inside a closed dock. Both continued from exact public recovery exports without repeating earned milestones or editing state. The original invasion performance sample was lost before flushing and is not claimed; a new90RAF sample during actual recapture measured p95≈16.7ms. Four paired orbit/surface scenes returned to242 geometries each time. `review.json`, both final `result.json` files and `artifact-cleanup.json` preserve provenance, limits, hashes and removed intermediate artifacts.

This proves a continuation of a played lineage, not a fresh-birth end-to-end campaign, all of milestone D, military loss/retreat variants, or human playtest/audio acceptance. E/adventures are deferred beyond the current goal.
